fix(test): the exit-code case arms a timeout it never reaches, and each loop run's holder ends with its run (brandon-menus-sjhy.irc)

A fired timeout concludes on the gone group as ok, so a timeout inside the
case's life hid a launch that waited for its holder.

fix(test): the launch-group cases end their holders by removing a path, and the timeout case samples a live group on a held clock (brandon-menus-sjhy.irc)

The abort and timeout cases each sample the group alive, end its member, then
act before the next poll. Every holder waits on the case's directory, which
afterEach removes, so no case bets on a holder's lifetime in real time.

fix(test): the launch-group abort case reaches its window by what it observes, not a sleep (brandon-menus-sjhy.irc)

The case means one state: the child ended, its group is gone, and the launch
has not yet sampled the group. A 1300 ms sleep aimed at it, so a loaded
machine saw the launch's own sample land first and read ok:true.

The case now launches on a held clock, so the launch samples the group only
when the case advances it. It waits, by condition, for the child's pidfile,
for the group's end, and for the launch to have seen the exit, then aborts
and advances. The holder outside the group, which keeps the child's close
from concluding first, lives until the case removes its directory, not for
3 s of real time.

The launcher's owner moves into launcherOn(clock), shared by the beforeEach
and this case.

feat(apply): session state has one writer; a run and a lane setup are effects (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.9kk) (#646)

* feat(apply): session state has one writer; a run and a lane setup are effects (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.9kk)

The session store refuses a write made while no journal turn is held, in
every daemon. A turn is synchronous, so a write while one is held is that
turn's own, and one check at the store's single write path is the whole
enforcement. The test-only view that refused such writes, its adapter
seam and the separate gauges field are gone.

The two writers left outside a turn now report through effect-done:

- A `run` click supersedes its sources in its turn, so they read pending
  from the click on, and describes the launch as a `run` effect. The
  performer runs the program behind the session's earlier effects; the
  run owner answers how it ended and no longer writes the bar.
- A lane setup is a `lane-setup` effect, settled by the click or the
  request that owes it and run by the performer. Its own per-session
  queue and defer are replaced by the performer's per-session order.

The check command, the demo and the doctor's command line build their
store with a holder that always holds, since each is one synchronous run.

* fix(apply): a request's arrival settles in its turn; a queued run is counted (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.9kk)

The lane setups a request's arrival settles were taken off the owed list
during the draw and reached the performer only once the draw had answered,
so a click made during the wait was performed ahead of them, and a draw that
threw lost them. The arrival (owed setups and the tmux status line) now
settles in the request's turn, measured as a click's switches are, and the
arm answers with the draw under way, so the turn's effects join the
session's order as the turn ends.

A run superseded by its click and still waiting behind the session's earlier
effects shows in the run stats as queued. The lane outcome's comment says
what underway now means, and a write's refusal text is built only when
refused.

* fix(apply): a request is drawn once applied; a run's sources resume whatever its launch did (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.9kk)

The request arm no longer draws: `applyRequest` applies the request and then
begins its draw, so a request whose apply rejected strands no draw. The
effects the request's turn described go on its render event.

A run's launch is awaited in a try/finally, so a launcher that throws still
resumes the run's sources and leaves nothing counted running.

The lane setup effect is declared by the lane setup owner, which the effect
union names from above, so the two no longer import each other.

* fix(apply): a queued lane setup is refused at close; every write asks for its turn first (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.9kk)

A lane setup waits in its session's effect order, so one still queued when
the daemon closes would start a restart no daemon is left to attach. The
lane setup owner closes with the daemon and refuses it as the close, as a
queued run is. A run the close aborted is answered as the close rather
than as a failure that only the teardown's order kept off the bar.

The store asks for the turn at the top of every public write, before an
empty batch or a held revision decides that nothing moves, so a write out
of its turn is refused whatever it would have written.
fix(draw): a frame's lanes are noted before its walk, so a frame that throws still says which lanes it drew for (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.0se)
refactor(draw): a view's draw returns the lane switches it drew under; two comments name lane frames (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.0se)

fix(facts): a replay draws the lane feeds and diagnostics the live draw was handed, and the frames a lane drew (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.0se)

A replay drew every frame with every lane idle, no open viewer, and only
the request answers, so a recording of a session with a lane following or
the warnings viewer open replayed a bar the user never saw.

- A draw line is one draw of the view, an answer or a lane's frame: it
  carries the instant it was drawn at and what it was handed (who it drew
  for, each lane's feed, the diagnostics list). A lane's frames write the
  view's frame memory and the session's effect memory, so the recorder
  notes each one, to every recording of the session, and the replay draws
  them in the file's order at their exact instants. RECORDING_VERSION 6.
- The daemon and the demo draw a view through one function (draw-view),
  which derives every draw projection from what the draw was handed and
  stands the open viewer in for the bar. The demo's own drawDsl call goes.
- A recording that holds only lane frames is kept and replays; `record`
  reports answers and lane frames.
- The seam test's live side is the daemon's draw throughout, and a new case
  replays a standing warning, a following lane, its toggles and the open
  viewer, compared whole.

feat(band): a switched-off band lane holds no follower process (candybar-animation-wbxz.w33)

The band mod stops its follow child on the daemon's SWITCHED_OFF answer
instead of keeping it alive to re-ask every 5s, and turning band (A) off
uninstalls the mod so sessions started afterwards never load it. An
uninstall of a mod that is not installed is the state off asks for, so it
is said rather than thrown.
